open_points.subject: Local Registry frontend authentication boundary
open_points.text: “The Registry frontend calls the API from the browser” / “the one staff credential into each tool acting as staff — the operator, a frontend server” / “How the frontend obtains the staff credential belongs to the frontend.”
open_points.question: For the local frontend’s staff actions, does the browser itself receive and hold the shared staff credential, or must those actions pass through a credential-holding server?
options: The browser holds and presents the staff credential
A frontend server holds the credential and proxies staff actions
The browser may perform only open reads
open_points.default_guess: A frontend server holds the credential and proxies every staff action.

open_points.subject: Operator agent trust boundary
open_points.text: “an agent preparing a client message for the owner (the WhatsApp link of the Factory's `AGENTS.md`)”
open_points.question: Does this agent or any external model/provider receive customer contact data, and if so, what named system and trust boundary governs that disclosure?
options: Contact data remains inside a local operator process
Contact data is disclosed to a named external agent provider
Only the owner receives the data and constructs the message
open_points.default_guess: Contact data remains inside a local process on Registry’s host and is not sent to an external model or provider.

open_points.subject: Credential transport on the host network
open_points.text: “They reach Registry over HTTP on the host's loopback or the host's internal network”
open_points.question: Are all co-resident processes and the host network trusted against observing credentials in transit, or must credential-bearing HTTP traffic have transport protection?
options: Trust the host and its internal network; plaintext HTTP is allowed
Require a protected local transport or authenticated proxy
open_points.default_guess: Trust the host OS and its internal network, allowing plaintext HTTP within that boundary.

open_points.subject: Publishing after withdrawal
open_points.text: “the previous published version of that type becomes `superseded`” / “Every accepted publish is a new version… the previous one is superseded”
open_points.question: When the latest version is already `withdrawn` and a new version is published, does the withdrawn version remain `withdrawn` or change to `superseded`?
options: It remains `withdrawn`; only a currently published pointer is superseded
open_points.default_guess: The withdrawn pointer remains `withdrawn`; only a currently published pointer becomes `superseded`.

open_points.subject: Invalid or incomplete instance configuration
open_points.text: “Service tokens, the staff credential, the artifact vocabulary (R0-08) and the frontend origin are the instance's configuration… a change takes effect when the instance restarts”
open_points.question: What observable behavior is required when the staff credential, frontend origin, or service-token mapping is missing, malformed, duplicated, or internally inconsistent at startup?
options: Refuse to start with a configuration error
Start with only affected capabilities disabled
Accept the configuration and reject affected requests at runtime
open_points.default_guess: Refuse to start and report a configuration error.

open_points.subject: Deployment-boundary verification
open_points.text: “The owner's deployment definition enforces this… and the owner checks it when deploying”
open_points.question: What concrete check produces evidence that Registry is unreachable beyond its host, and what must happen when that check fails?
options: An automated deployment check blocks completion
A documented manual check records pass or failure
The deployment definition alone is considered sufficient
open_points.default_guess: An automated reachability or published-port check fails the deployment when the boundary is violated.
